audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Neeko, Skill, Riven, Riven, Neeko, Riven, Riven while the packet chart reads Skill, Neeko, Neeko, Neeko, Neeko, Neeko, Riven - five of seven rows are wrong, including Level 1, which the page hands to Neeko while its own why calls it a genuine fifty-fifty.
audit.why: Every one of the page's whys already describes the packet chart and contradicts the token above it: whys[0] 'a genuine fifty-fifty' (Skill), whys[1] 'she dictates when trades happen' (Neeko), whys[2] 'a coin-flip that costs you HP' (Neeko), whys[3] 'she is outscaling your lane pressure' (Neeko), whys[5] 'Neeko still bursts harder at first-item' (Neeko), whys[6] 'two items and her burst no longer kills you' (Riven). The 55.13% overall win rate is not in conflict: Neeko owns the lane phase and Riven owns everything after two items, which is exactly what the corrected chart says. The neeko__riven mirror set the same seven values.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 2, 3 and 5 flipped as one atomic paired group in both layers to Skill, Neeko, Neeko, Neeko, Neeko, Neeko, Riven, with ratings moved to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: The early-game advice tells you to approach from the side of the wave 'so any E she throws hits minions first and breaks apart before reaching you'. That is backwards, and a player who follows it walks into the worst version of the ability.
audit.why: Riot's text for Tangle-Barbs: 'If the tangle kills an enemy or passes through a champion, it becomes larger, faster, and roots for longer.' Minions do not stop it - they empower it. Standing behind the wave is the single worst place to be against a Neeko who is fishing. The only thing that beats Tangle-Barbs is sidestepping the cast line itself.
audit.corrected: The early prose and the Level 2-3 spike now say the root grows off minions and that sidestepping the line is the answer.

audit.whatIsWrong: The ultimate is called 'Popup Blossom' in whys[4], the Level 6 spike, the mid prose, the late prose and wants.foe[1], and is described as a 'full-channel AOE stun'.
audit.why: The real name is Pop Blossom. Riot's text: after a short preparation she leaps, knocking up all nearby enemies, and on landing damages and stuns them - a knockup into a stun at 600 range, not a channel you can simply walk out of. The line that actually matters is the last one: 'The preparation is hidden if Neeko is disguised.' Combined with Inherent Glamour, that means the ordinary visual tell is absent exactly when the ult is most likely to kill you.
audit.corrected: Name corrected everywhere, and the hidden-preparation interaction written into the Level 6 spike, whys[4], the mid prose and wants.foe[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly says 'track her E cooldown' without ever giving the number.
audit.why: Tangle-Barbs is 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s and Blooming Burst is 9/8.5/8/7.5/7s - so the root window narrows to ten seconds by rank 5, which is why the lane gets harder rather than easier through Levels 4-5.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns written into whys[3], the Level 2-3 spike and the early prose.

edits.before: Neeko has the cleaner Level 1 — her Blooming Burst (Q) pokes for free at range and you have no reliable answer without burning E into a root she can already throw. Accept that Level 1 is a farm check, not a fight. At Level 2 her Tangle-Barbs (E) changes everything: she can root you through the wave and immediately layer Q damage before your shield (E) even lands. Do not straight-line walk at her — approach from the side of the wave so any E she throws hits minions first and breaks apart before reaching you. Level 3 does not flip the lane; she has all three abilities and can clone-disguise to bait your all-in onto the wrong target. Sit on the lead she hands you through farm, track her E cooldown religiously, and accept that early lane pressure belongs to her.
edits.after: Neeko has the cleaner Level 1 — Blooming Burst (Q) pokes for free at range and you have no answer without burning Valor into a root she can already throw. Accept that Level 1 is a farm check, not a fight. At Level 2 Tangle-Barbs (E) changes everything: it roots through the wave and grows larger, faster and longer-rooting for every unit it kills, so standing behind minions feeds it rather than stopping it. Do not straight-line at her — sidestep the cast line itself, because nothing else beats it. Level 3 does not flip the lane; Shapesplitter steers a clone mid-flight to bait your all-in onto nothing. Farm the lead she hands you, count the 12-second E, and accept that early pressure is hers.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are her ownership window — Neeko's AP is scaling, her E root gets longer at later ranks, and Popup Blossom (R) at Level 6 is a channelled AOE stun that will kill you if she hits it. Play the wave: freeze near your tower so she must walk into turret range to poke, deny her the open-lane patterns that let her land E for free, and respect every brush near your side. When you see her back off or waste E into a minion, that is your window — dash in with Q-direction-steered to come in from an angle, land W stun before she can root you, and finish the chain. Your R at 6 is meaningful but only if you can complete the combo; a Neeko who is ready will jump-channel R the moment you close, so commit only when you are certain she has no clean stun angle.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 are her ownership window — Neeko's AP is scaling, Tangle-Barbs roots longer at later ranks, and Pop Blossom (R) at Level 6 knocks you up and then stuns, lethal inside 600 units. Play the wave: freeze near your tower so she must walk into turret range to poke, deny her the open-lane angles that let her land E for free, and respect every brush on your side. When she backs off or throws E into nothing, that is your window — steer Broken Wings in from an angle, land Ki Burst before she can root you, and finish the chain. Blade of the Exile at 6 matters only if you complete the combo; while she is disguised the R preparation never shows, so commit only when she has no stun angle.

edits.before: Two items changes the maths permanently in your favour. Neeko's burst rotation — E root into Q charges into R — cannot one-shot you through Immortal Shieldbow's shield and the raw HP of your build, and once she burns her combo you can close with Q chain, land W stun, and execute with Wind Slash. She is squishy and has no real disengage tool once E is on cooldown; every fight she walks into past laning phase is a potential death. Respect her picks and AOE threat in team fights — never stand in a clump she can Popup Blossom — but in side-lane and 1v1 situations your sustained damage and healing outlast her burst window comfortably. Win condition: survive the lane, hit two items, and punish every overextension with the full combo.
edits.after: Two items changes the maths permanently in your favour. notes: 'Popup Blossom' is the same class of fabricated name as the calibration examples and appeared five times; the real name is Pop Blossom, and the packet's suspectNames caught only one of the five instances. The more damaging error was tactical: the early prose told the reader to hide behind minions from Tangle-Barbs, when Riot's text says the tangle grows larger, faster and longer-rooting for every unit it kills. Chart rows 0, 1, 2, 3 and 5 proposed as one atomic paired group to match the packet and the neeko__riven mirror; the 55.13% win rate is not in conflict, since Neeko owns the lane and Riven owns the two-item game. Full layer calls Neeko 'he' in tldr, tradeGood, tradeBad, ahead, breakdown.feeding, breakdown.late, dontsFull[0].d and report[11].t, and calls Riven 'he' in places too - I did not edit those because they contain mojibake em-dashes that risk a before-mismatch. Recommend one encoding-safe sweep for the pronouns across this champion.
